answer: The pulse graph is rebuilt each epoch, so that the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the terrace audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the horizon checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 6 times its size, so a group of 17 keys loses far more than 17 single identities would. That is 23 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
